qt: to the Commission Nikolaos Anadiotis (NI) Subject:

The Holy Synod of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church confirmed that at least 60 Orthodox Christians were killed on 20 and 24 October 2026 in attacks which took place in the Merti and Sirka districts in Ethiopia’s Oromia regional state. At least 20 homes were set on fire and 20 people were left seriously injured. The perpetrators have not yet been identified1. I pointed out the attacks against Christian communities in Ethiopia in question Ε002439/20262. In the answer she gave on 3 August 20263, Vice-President / High Representative Kaja Kallas said the EU is monitoring the situation, calling for accountability and systematically raising the issue of religious freedom in its political dialogue with Ethiopia. The Ethiopian Human Rights Commission had already recorded repeated attacks in these same areas, calling for effective measures to protect civilians4. In addition, the EU provided EUR 609 million in funding for Ethiopia for the period 2024-2027. The funding was intended for governance, including peace-building5. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
What specific actions did it take after 3 August 2026 and what was the outcome?
Will it ask the Ethiopian authorities for specific protection measures, an independent investigation into these fresh attacks, and an accountability timeline?
Will it link relevant funding programmes to verifiable criteria for the protection of religious communities, without this affecting humanitarian aid?
